title: Linguistic Cost Mapping Panel — token-level attribution & export UX
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Design and prototype a dedicated panel in Redwood Console that maps cost down to linguistic primitives (token-level) and makes attribution and export workflows first-class. The panel surfaces per-request token breakdowns (system/user/assistant/tool), aggregated model-slices (by model, quantization profile, sequence length bucket), and role-aware filters for org-level chargeback. Exports should support CSV and newline-delimited JSON with configurable columns for downstream billing systems. This ticket covers: interaction patterns, export schema, visualizations (stacked bars + sparklines + lightweight Sankey for flow from prompts -> functions -> responses), microcopy, and an accessibility pass. Backend contract and telemetry keys are enumerated in dependencies.

design_notes: Export schema should default to anonymized user identifiers and provide an opt-in toggle for raw user identifiers (enterprise only, requires security review).
Token kinds: system, user, assistant, tool/function. Provide both absolute counts and relative percentages per request row.

Preset export columns: minimal (request_id, timestamp, cost_usd), billing-ready (request_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, token_role_breakdown, cost_usd, workspace_id, hashed_actor_id), forensic (includes prompt_preview - redacted if sensitivity toggle on).

Visualization rules: stacked bars use saturated hues with high contrast; sparklines show 30-day rolling median; expandable details use monospace for token counts and a badge for top-3 prompt tokens by frequency.
Rollout plan: behind feature flag 'lcmp_v1' for 10% of orgs in Beta, collect performance telemetry on export job completion times and panel render times.
open_questions: Should we include raw prompt text in the forensic export for enterprise audited accounts? (security + legal signoff required)
What is acceptable export throughput (rows/min) before we gate CSV generation to an async job? Engineering to advise (ENG-5899).
Do cost buckets need to map to multiple ratecards (hosted vs dedicated) in the same export, or should we normalize to a single USD column?
